physics_goals.quote: PHOBOS consisted of many silicon detectors surrounding the interaction region. With these detectors, physicists are able to count the total number of produced particles and study their angular distribution.
physics_goals.value: Count the total number of produced charged particles and study their angular distribution in a very large number of unselected collisions, looking for unusual events and fluctuations

summary.plain: PHOBOS was a compact RHIC experiment at Brookhaven that surrounded the collision point with silicon detectors to count nearly all the charged particles made in each gold-gold collision, plus two small spectrometers. It ran from 2000 to 2005.
summary.technical: PHOBOS: array of silicon pad and strip detectors for charged-particle multiplicity over almost the full solid angle, two magnetic spectrometers for particle identification near mid-rapidity, plus time-of-flight walls and trigger counters; ran at RHIC 2000-2005 (Au+Au, d+Au, p+p, Cu+Cu) and made the first RHIC multiplicity measurements.
